P1.evidence: The weakest open in the batch and the only one with no frame at all. There was a KL setter and no notes were read back. After brief small talk about Georgian food the rep went straight to 'Well, I know we have a limited amount of time. You ready to just jump right in?' and the prospect immediately began his own story. None of the four frame parts were set, so there was no frame to agree to, and the open question was never asked - the rep got the opening information because the prospect volunteered it. Note this is the call taken immediately before a one-to-one in which the rep told his manager his discovery stays too surface-level; the absence of any frame here is the upstream cause.

P2.evidence: Age was asked but only at 00:16:38, buried inside the pitch as a setup for the dysfunctional-movement argument rather than as baseline; height and weight were never asked at all, on a call where the presenting goal is losing belly fat. Work was the cleanest check of the batch - 'do you work at a desk or are you doing something physical?' is the check almost verbatim. Health conditions and injuries were never asked in any form. Training frequency, duration and content were covered well, and the six-month plateau was properly established. Diet was asked - 'Do you like track your macros or things like that or no?' - and produced something significant: the prospect deliberately stays hungry, skips breakfast, eats nothing after 6 or 7pm, and does it on the basis of 'I read it somewhere or someone's told to me that when you feel hungry, your organism, it's your fat.' The rep responded 'Okay, wow. Hmm' and moved on without exploring what he actually eats or addressing the belief. Sleep and energy were never asked.

P3.evidence: The bridge question deserves credit: the rep asked for a deeper motivation three separate times, in three different phrasings - 'is there anything going on just in your life, maybe outside of boredom?', 'what I was asked for is, do you have any other reason that you're wanting to improve your fitness in general?', and earlier 'is there another part of your life that you want to build up the endurance for?' That is persistence, and the script asks for it. The prospect refused all three: 'No, just to be a healthy guy. That's it' and 'No, no, just want to be fit, you know, and that's it.' What did not happen is what should follow a refusal. Nobody asked who else this impacts, nobody drove toward family, identity or longevity beyond the prospect's own passing remark about 'bigger ages', and no reflect-back reframed boredom into anything with weight. The summary at 00:13:43 restated the features accurately and added nothing.

P4.evidence: Barely run. The only past-attempts question was narrow - 'have you ever worked with some, like, an online trainer in any fitness?' - which established he has used in-person gym trainers but never explored what those trainers did, what results came of it, or why he stopped. The six-month plateau is a failure sitting in plain view and nobody asked why it happened, what he changed, or what he thinks is causing it beyond his own 'I don't know what it is, to be honest.' No gap was named by either party, and the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' move never ran.

P5.evidence: Not run - the seventh and final consecutive sales call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent. This is the call where its absence is most consequential rather than least. The prospect had no stated motivation and the rep knew it, having asked three times. P5 is the phase that manufactures the missing weight, and the sales manager had described the exact move for this profile the day before - challenging a comfortable prospect on what staying comfortable is costing him. None of it ran, and the call defaulted to discounting instead.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The rep moved from the end of the pitch straight into pricing when the prospect asked, with no belief question, no all-in question and no verbal yes taken beforehand. Because no commitment existed, the price objection arrived with nothing behind it and the only available response was to lower the number.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected. The Primal University link was offered but not confirmed as sent. Onboarding with Trevor, the agreement email and the welcome sequence were never reached.

objection_plays.detail: Two good diagnostic questions ran - 'is it just like, is it the price is just more than you want to spend?' and 'I mean, like how much were you expecting?' - and the second is a genuinely useful move not even in the script. But the prospect answered neither ('I didn't think about that, to be honest') and the rep proceeded to discount anyway, which is the reverse of the play. Nothing else ran: no isolate, no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no permission to talk openly about finances, and not one of the six financial picture areas - cash on hand, monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, used versus available, investments. The offer to break payment up came before any of the information that is supposed to shape it, and was followed within the same exchange by a lower tier and then an improvised $1,500 entry point.

Trigger was explicit and early: 'I have to think about it. I can't give you an answer right now.' No scripted move ran at all - no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no final 'are you sure'. The rep's response to the deferral was to take a phone number and then reduce the price twice, which trades a decision for a discount without ever finding out what the decision was about.
No timing objection. The prospect wanted to change now and had already tried a home kettlebell session before the call.
No spousal or partner consult raised. Family status was never explored.
No fear or doubt objection surfaced. He was confident in the approach, having felt the effect of a single home session.

The central situation on this call has no scripted play: a prospect with no gap and no why, who declines three direct invitations to supply one. Every phase from P3 onward assumes a motivation exists to be deepened, and the playbook has no branch for what to do when the honest answer is boredom. The manager articulated a verbal approach for exactly this profile the day before - challenging the comfortable position and asking what being a seven rather than a ten is costing them - but it exists nowhere in the written process, so it did not run. A second unscripted trigger sits inside discovery: a prospect deliberately restricting food on a mistaken belief, which is both a live coaching opportunity and a credibility win, and was met with 'Okay, wow. Hmm.'

notes: No frame, no root cause, no consequence frame and no commitment check, followed by a price ladder from $6,000 to a $1,500 entry in about four minutes. The bridge question was asked three times and that persistence is worth keeping. Coach two things: when a prospect answers the why-now with boredom, that is the cue to run P5 hardest rather than to move to price, and never introduce a lower number before the financial picture questions have been asked and answered.
